gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Synology's 14.6 dB(A) noise rating for the DS223 was measured with Synology SATA SSDs, while the DS223j (18.2 dB(A)) and DS225+ (19.6 dB(A)) were measured with hard drives. The DS223's 'quietest' number therefore doesn't apply to the two-HDD Time Machine build ChatGPT told the shopper to buy.
standout_why: Apple's page (cited) covers only SMB support and AFP not being supported in macOS 27 or later. The Synology Time Machine KB page (cited) gave no body text when fetched. The Synology compare pages (results 4–9, not cited) show 14.6 / 18.2 / 19.6 dB(A) side by side. Each figure's drive condition is in a separate footnote, and nothing points out that the DS223's figure uses SSDs. Laptopbee calls the DS223 'the quietest NAS I tested' and 'silent operation even during backups' but gives no dB figure and doesn't say which drives were installed. Android Central's visible text has no noise or power figures and doesn't name Time Machine.
decides: This weakens the DS223's claim to be the quiet pick. With hard drives, which ChatGPT's own plan uses, Synology publishes no DS223 noise figure. The only HDD-based Synology figures are the DS223j at 18.2 dB(A) and the DS225+ at 19.6 dB(A), so the honest comparison is closer than 14.6 vs 19.6. Power figures are also stated on different bases: Synology gives 'access' and 'HDD hibernation' watts, and QNAP gives 'operating (typical)' and 'HDD standby' watts 'with drives fully populated'. Igor'sLAB measured the UGREEN DXP2800 with only one NVMe SSD installed. So no single watt figure ranks these boxes for a 24/7 Time Machine target. The DS223 vs DS225+ choice still comes down to networking and warranty (2 vs 3 years), not quietness.

findings.label: Rated noise and test drives
findings.value: 14.6 dB(A), idle, measured with Synology SATA SSDs
findings.note: Footnote: 'Noise testing was conducted with the Synology system fully installed with Synology SATA SSDs and in an idle state.' Two GRAS 40AE microphones at 1 m, front and rear. Background noise was 16.49–17.51 dB(A), so the rated figure is below the test room's own background noise. The en-uk page (https://www.synology.com/en-uk/products/DS223) has the same SSD footnote. A search snippet claimed the DS223 footnote names Seagate 2TB HDDs, but neither page I opened says that.

findings.label: Measured noise (reviewer)
findings.value: 33.2 dB(A) idle; 35.6 dB(A) load, at 40 cm
findings.source_title: Ugreen NASync DXP2800 NAS im Test – igor'sLAB (Tim Kutzner)
findings.note: Voltcraft SL-200 meter, 40 cm, fan in Lo mode. The test drives aren't stated. The room column reads 33.2 dB(A), the same as the idle figure, so idle may be at the room's noise floor. The 40 cm distance is not Synology's 1 m. A free-field estimate (20·log10(1/0.4) ≈ 8 dB) would put it near 25 dB(A) at 1 m. That is an approximation, not a measurement.

findings.label: Measured power (reviewer)
findings.value: 5.6 W standby; 14.5 W during data transfer; 0.6 W off with Wake-on-LAN
findings.source_title: Ugreen NASync DXP2800 NAS im Test – igor'sLAB (Tim Kutzner)
findings.note: Measured at the wall with only one NVMe SSD installed. The author removed the other drives on purpose. This can't be compared with Synology's figures, which include fully loaded HDD bays.

findings.label: Third-party HDDs under DSM 7.3 (2025 Plus series)
findings.value: Unlisted SATA HDDs can create storage pools on 2025 DiskStation Plus models with no 'unverified' warning. Unlisted M.2 NVMe drives still can't be used for a new cache or pool.
findings.source_title: The Synology Hard Drive and SSD Support Change in DSM 7.3 Explained – NASCompares (Rob Andrews, 2025-10-08)
findings.note: The article body names the DS1525+, DS925+ and DS725+ but not the DS225+. The DS225+ is a 2025 Plus model, so this very likely applies, but I couldn't read a Synology page confirming it for the DS225+. The DS225+ product page only says 'Synology only guarantees full functionality… for compatible drives.'
